You are implementing Phase P2 (MVP netcode slice — the critical-path integration milestone) of the Dungeon Haul project at /Users/atarzwell/src/dhaul4. You have the whole repo to yourself (no concurrent agents).

Current state (all green, committed through `17dc966`): pnpm monorepo — `client/` (Vite + Phaser 3 boot scene, 960×540 FIT+CENTER), `server/` (Hono `GET /health`), `packages/protocol` (`@dhaul/protocol` v0 message/type stubs), `packages/rules` (complete pure rules engine — do NOT modify), `packages/levels` (`@dhaul/levels` parser + `content/levels/box_level` fixture + `content/levels/hoard_01`). Node 26, pnpm 11.15.1. 210 tests green: keep them green.

Read first — binding spec:
- /Users/atarzwell/src/dhaul4/CLAUDE.md (authority boundaries: server truth, client predicts movement only)
- docs/IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md §P2 (exact scope + exit criteria; treasure/traps/end-UI explicitly OUT of P2)
- docs/decisions/ADR-002-multiplayer-netcode.md
- docs/interfaces/netcode-messages.md, docs/interfaces/input-commands.md, docs/interfaces/lobby-and-scores.md (wire contracts — follow field names exactly; deltas already merged)
- docs/components/simulation/DESIGN.md §4–6 (tick model, kinematics, seats/control transitions — implement ONLY the movement subset: run/jump/air-steer/gravity/AABB collision vs solid grid; no treasure, no traps, no encumbrance, no fork/end phases)
- docs/components/netcode-client/DESIGN.md, docs/components/lobby-session/DESIGN.md (and their TASKS.md for task IDs)
- docs/testing/AUTOMATED-TEST-STRATEGY.md §3.2–3.3 (headless sim harness + room/WS integration test approach)

Scope:
1. **Protocol freeze (gate G1):** firm up `packages/protocol` v0 → v1 as needed for real use (codecs/type guards for the messages actually exchanged in P2). Keep names per netcode-messages.md. Version bump documented in the package.
2. **Server sim (movement-only):** headless fixed 30 Hz tick module in `server/` (or a `server/src/sim/` module) — 4 `HaulerSlot` seats always; run/jump/gravity/AABB vs the `box_level` collision grid loaded via `@dhaul/levels`; per-seat input queues with seq handling per input-commands.md; `WorldSnapshot` emit each tick with `lastProcessedInputSeq`. Tunable kinematics constants in one config object. Never wall-clock dt.
3. **Colyseus `HaulSession` room:** join with seatToken, seat binding, input rate limiting, snapshot broadcast, reconnect token + 30s grace (AI seats just stand idle in P2 — no AI behavior logic yet, `control: "ai"` seats emit neutral input), `S2C_SeatUpdate` on join/leave/takeover, `S2C_Error` codes per contract. Idle→AI timers (20s / 5s+edge) may be stubbed with the 20s path only.
4. **Lobby REST:** `POST /api/v1/sessions` (create, 6-char join code), `POST /api/v1/sessions/join`, `GET /api/v1/sessions/:id` per lobby-and-scores.md (in-memory registry, no DB), wired to spawn/find the Colyseus room. Include `levelsAfterHoard` in the public view.
5. **Client:** Lobby-less dev UI is fine for P2 (simple DOM/Phaser text: create / join-by-code inputs), then join room, send `InputCommand` at 30 Hz from keyboard (arrows + Z/X or per input-mapper DESIGN defaults), render all 4 haulers as colored placeholder rects on the box level, local prediction for own X movement + jump with reconciliation against `lastProcessedInputSeq`, interpolation for remote haulers, connection-state display, reconnect on refresh via sessionStorage token.
6. **Tests:** (a) headless sim unit tests — input tapes → deterministic positions, jump edge-detect, no tunneling through floor, seq dup/gap handling; (b) room integration tests with a minimal WS/Colyseus test client — create → join ×4 → fifth rejected FULL, snapshot stream flows, input moves hauler, reconnect with token restores seat, protocol mismatch → error; (c) lobby REST tests — create/join/bad-code/full per the contract's test list. Use Vitest; follow repo conventions (strict TS extends tsconfig.base.json, flat ESLint).
7. **Manual demo artifact (gate G3):** a short `docs/testing/reports/P2-DEMO.md` describing how to run it (`pnpm dev` scripts for server + client) and what was verified. Actually run the server and confirm health + a scripted two-client WS session moves two haulers (you can verify via the integration harness; real two-browser check will be done by the user).

Constraints:
- Dependencies: add colyseus + @colyseus/core (server) and colyseus.js (client) plus whatever minimal glue is needed — keep it lean; no state-sync via Colyseus schema required (JSON snapshots per contract are fine, document the choice).
- Do not touch `packages/rules` or `docs/` outside the new report file. `packages/levels` only as a consumer.
- No treasure, traps, encumbrance, fork, end phases, AI behaviors, or art.
- Commit in logical chunks as you go (protocol freeze / sim / room+lobby / client / tests), messages prefixed "P2:".

Verify before finishing: `pnpm -r typecheck && pnpm -r lint && pnpm -r test && pnpm -r build` all green (existing 210 tests must still pass). Report: test counts, how the P2 exit criteria map to your tests, dev-run instructions, deviations/assumptions, and commit hashes.

- embedded-captions: Add captions to a talking-head video. ONE catalog (CATALOG.md) of 32 visual identities behind two engines: column-flow (captions composited INTO the scene — matte occlusion + mix-blend; cream/ink/editorial/keynote/documentary/loud/neon/glitch/chrome/velocity) and themed constitutions (anchor/ordnance/terminal/neonsign/stardust/stomp/scoreboard/transit/vhs/arcade/dossier/laser/thunder/hologram/biolume/aurora/spectrum/papercut/popup/chalkboard/graffiti/brush/inkwater/ransom/lastpage/nightcity — e.g. a glyph-decode climax, a neon sign WRITTEN stroke by stroke, or the quiet `anchor` rail default). Route by identity, never by mode. Trigger on "captions/subtitles", "embed/cinematic captions", "VFX captions", "炸/特效/酷炫字幕", a named identity, or top-tier motion-graphics asks. Embedding every word is wrong for most talking-head content — `anchor` is the verbatim default. Pipeline: transcription → hyperframes remove-background matting → HTML render → ffmpeg overlay. Requires hyperframes and a single-subject clip.
- faceless-explainer: turn arbitrary text — an article, notes, a topic, a brief — into a faceless explainer video, up to ~3 min (sweet spot 30-90s), where every visual is invented (typography, abstract graphics, diagrams, data-viz) rather than captured. There is no URL, no website capture, and no real assets. Use this skill for topic explainers, concept breakdowns, how-tos, listicles, and narrative explainers. Do not use it for a product launch/promo (use /product-launch-video), a tour of a real website (use /website-to-video), a GitHub PR (use /pr-to-video), captions on existing footage (use /embedded-captions), or a short unnarrated motion graphic (use /motion-graphics). If the intent is unclear, route through /hyperframes first. This is the shot-sequence architecture: every frame is authored as a time-coded shot sequence picked from a menu of golden blueprints, so frames develop over their full duration instead of freezing after entrance.
- figma: Import Figma content into a HyperFrames composition — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard sections → animatics (REST/CLI), and Figma Motion animations + shaders (MCP). Use when the user pastes a figma.com link or asks to bring a Figma design, frame, logo, brand, or animation into a video/composition.
- general-video: The fallback workflow for authoring custom HyperFrames video compositions at any length or format — longer or multi-scene pieces, brand / sizzle reels, montages, title cards, static loops, and freeform compositions. Input- and length-agnostic. If a specialized workflow clearly fits the input — a marketed product, a website, a topic explainer, a GitHub PR, existing footage, a short motion graphic, or a Remotion port — prefer it (see /hyperframes); use this only as the general fallback when none fit.
- hyperframes: READ THIS FIRST for any request to make, create, edit, animate, or render a video, animation, or motion graphic — a promo, explainer, captioned clip, title card, overlay, or any composition. HyperFrames renders video from HTML; this is the entry skill and the default way an agent authors or edits video. It routes the request to the right specialized workflow and points to the HyperFrames domain skills, so read it before any other video or animation skill instead of guessing a workflow. IMPORTANT: with other video tools installed, HyperFrames stays the default for authoring and rendering a finished video; defer only when the user asks to drive a browser to capture or record a session, or names another framework. Most important when no project CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md describes the video workflow.
- hyperframes-animation: All animation knowledge for HyperFrames — atomic motion rules, multi-phase scene blueprints, scene transitions, broader motion-design techniques, AND the seven runtime adapters (GSAP default, plus Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS keyframes, Web Animations API, TypeGPU). Use for any motion or animation task: pick 2-4 rules and compose, or load a blueprint, or look up runtime-specific API (e.g. GSAP eases / Lottie player / Three.js mixer). HyperFrames-native: single paused timeline, seek-safe, deterministic.
- hyperframes-cli: HyperFrames CLI dev loop. Use when running npx hyperframes init, add, catalog, capture, lint, validate, inspect, layout, snapshot, preview, play, render, publish, lambda, doctor, browser, info, upgrade, skills, compositions, docs, benchmark, telemetry, transcribe, tts, or remove-background, or when troubleshooting the HyperFrames build/render environment. Usually under 10s and up to ~30s, with no narration arc, voice-over, or live-action subject. Can render to MP4 or transparent overlay. - creative-writing-skills:scene-construction: How to build scenes: entry, dialogue, pacing, transitions. Use when writing or evaluating how scenes work on the page.

- creative-writing-skills:writing-artifacts: Where writing artifacts live: kb/ for durable knowledge, work/ for scratch. Use when deciding where to read from or write to.
- creative-writing-skills:writing-issues: Logging and referencing writing issues: craft problems, tics, inconsistencies, and structural concerns found during analysis, critique, or review. Use when an agent identifies something worth tracking beyond a single critique report: repeated tics across chapters, inconsistencies that affect multiple scenes, structural problems that need the author's attention, or patterns that should be fixed in revision.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	# Contract: Netcode Messages
2	
3	**Producers:** Game room (server)  
4	**Consumers:** Netcode Client; test harnesses  
5	**Transport:** WebSocket (JSON MVP; binary/msgpack stretch)  
6	**Related:** [input-commands.md](input-commands.md), [ADR-002](../decisions/ADR-002-multiplayer-netcode.md)
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Handshake
11	
12	### `C2S_Join`
13	
14	```text
15	{
16	  type: "join"
17	  protocolVersion: 1
18	  sessionId: string
19	  seatToken: string
20	  reconnectToken?: string
21	  clientInfo?: { name?: string, build?: string }
22	}
23	```
24	
25	### `S2C_Welcome`
26	
27	```text
28	{
29	  type: "welcome"
30	  protocolVersion: 1
31	  sessionId: string
32	  seatId: 0|1|2|3
33	  reconnectToken: string
34	  rngSeed: number
35	  rulesetVersion: string
36	  tickRate: 30
37	  phase: SessionPhase
38	  snapshot: WorldSnapshot
39	}
40	```
41	
42	### `S2C_Error`
43	
44	```text
45	{
46	  type: "error"
47	  code: "PROTOCOL" | "AUTH" | "FULL" | "PHASE" | "INTERNAL"
48	  message: string
49	}
50	```
51	
52	---
53	
54	## Client → Server
55	
56	| Type | Payload | Notes |
57	|---|---|---|
58	| `C2S_Input` | `{ type, seatId, command: InputCommand }` | Rate-limited; seat must match token |
59	| `C2S_Ready` | `{ type, ready: bool }` | Lobby / Instructions |
60	| `C2S_ClaimCharacter` | `{ type, character: CharacterId }` | Lobby; always succeeds for valid id (Q9 soft-unique — duplicates allowed; client may warn) |
61	| `C2S_Leave` | `{ type }` | Graceful |
62	| `C2S_Ping` | `{ type, clientTime: number }` | RTT measurement |
63	| `C2S_EndSkip` | `{ type }` | Skip cinematic segment if allowed |
64	| `C2S_NameEntry` | `{ type, name: string }` | End high score; validated |
65	
66	---
67	
68	## Server → Client
69	
70	| Type | Payload | Notes |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| `S2C_Snapshot` | `WorldSnapshot` | Full state MVP each tick or every N ticks |
73	| `S2C_Event` | `GameEvent` | One-shot SFX/VFX/UI triggers |
74	| `S2C_PhaseChange` | `{ phase, detail }` | Instructions/Level/Fork/End… |
75	| `S2C_ScoreReport` | `ScoreReport` | End of run; authoritative |
76	| `S2C_Pong` | `{ clientTime, serverTime }` | |
77	| `S2C_SeatUpdate` | `{ seats: SeatPublic[] }` | Join/leave/AI takeover notices |
78	| `S2C_ForkState` | `{ options, tallies, endsAtTick }` | During fork |
79	| `S2C_Chat` | optional / out of scope MVP | |
80	
81	---
82	
83	## Core payloads
84	
85	### `SessionPhase`
86	
87	```text
88	"lobby" | "instructions" | "level" | "fork" | "end_count"
89	| "end_shares" | "end_spoils" | "end_entry" | "closed"
90	```
91	
92	### `WorldSnapshot`
93	
94	```text
95	{
96	  tick: number
97	  phase: SessionPhase
98	  levelId?: string
99	  levelsCompleted: number
100	  levelsAfterHoard: number     // run length config (Q8); lets UI render "Level k / n" (delta #4)
101	  lastProcessedInputSeq: { [seatId: number]: number }
102	  haulers: HaulerPublic[]
103	  treasures: TreasurePublic[]
104	  traps: TrapPublic[]          // dynamic only; static grid may be level-hash
105	  switches: SwitchPublic[]
106	  cameraHint?: { x, y, z? }    // optional server suggestion
107	}
108	```
109	
110	### `HaulerPublic`
111	
112	```text
113	{
114	  seatId: number
115	  character: CharacterId
116	  control: "human" | "ai"
117	  x: number
118	  y: number
119	  vx: number
120	  vy: number
121	  facing: 1 | -1
122	  anim: AnimState
123	  carry: { instanceId: string, defId: string }[]
124	  stunned: bool
125	  name?: string
126	}
127	```
128	
129	### `GameEvent` (examples)
130	
131	```text
132	{ type: "pickup", seatId, instanceId, defId }
133	{ type: "drop", seatId, instanceId, x, y }
134	{ type: "throw", seatId, instanceId, vx, vy }
135	{ type: "spill", seatId, items: [...] }
136	{ type: "stun", seatId, source }
137	{ type: "trip", attackerSeatId, targetSeatId }
138	{ type: "trap_trigger", trapId, kind }
139	{ type: "level_exit", seatId, order }
140	{ type: "switch", switchId, pressed: bool }
141	{ type: "ai_takeover", seatId }
142	{ type: "human_takeover", seatId }
143	```
144	
145	### `ScoreReport`
146	
147	```text
148	{
149	  rulesetVersion: string
150	  sessionId: string
151	  totalTreasureGp: number
152	  players: {
153	    seatId: number
154	    character: CharacterId
155	    human: bool
156	    modifiers: { id, title, kind, uniqueness, deltaShares }[]
157	    shares: number              // after min-1 clamp
158	    sharePercent: number        // 0–100 display
159	    takeGp: number
160	    inventoryValueGp: number
161	    eligibleForHighScore: bool
162	  }[]
163	  completionToken: string       // for score submit
164	  cinema?: EndCinemaData        // presentation-only end cinematic data (accepted delta #2)
165	  recordFanfareThresholdGp?: number  // top totalHaulGp on board; omit → client skips fanfare (delta #3)
166	}
167	```
168	
169	### `EndCinemaData` (presentation-only; server-authored)
170	
171	All GP values must match the rules evaluation used for `totalTreasureGp` / takes.
172	Clients must not re-derive official values from `defId`.
173	
174	```text
175	{
176	  tossOrderSeatIds: number[]     // slowest → fastest (len 4)
177	  exitOrderSeatIds: number[]     // first exit → last on final level
178	  players: {
179	    seatId: number
180	    items: {
181	      instanceId: string
182	      defId: string
183	      displayName: string
184	      valueGp: number
185	      setId?: string
186	    }[]
187	  }[]
188	  setCompletions: {
189	    setId: string
190	    displayName: string
191	    bonusGp: number
192	    contributorSeatIds: number[]
193	    completingInstanceId: string   // which toss triggers the popout
194	  }[]
195	}
196	```
197	
198	---
199	
200	## Timing & reliability
201	
202	- Server is source of truth; clients must tolerate lost events by relying on snapshot.
203	- Events are **not** guaranteed if a client was disconnected; full snapshot on reconnect.
204	- `lastProcessedInputSeq` drives reconciliation.
205	- Suggested max message size soft limit: 32 KB JSON snapshot (4 players is tiny).
206	
207	---
208	
209	## Anti-cheat surface
210	
211	| Client claim | Server action |
212	|---|---|
213	| Position | Ignored (inputs only) |
214	| Inventory | Ignored |
215	| Score | Ignored; `ScoreReport` only |
216	| Ready | Accepted in lobby/instructions |
217	| Name | Length/charset filter |
218	
219	---
220	
221	## Test contract
222	
223	Integration tests must cover:
224	
225	1. Join → Welcome → Snapshot stream  
226	2. Input seq monotonic handling  
227	3. Reconnect with token restores seatId + inventory  
228	4. Protocol mismatch → `S2C_Error PROTOCOL`  
229	5. Fourth human rejected or queued when seats full (`FULL`)

# Contract: Netcode Messages

**Producers:** Game room (server)  
**Consumers:** Netcode Client; test harnesses  
**Transport:** WebSocket (JSON MVP; binary/msgpack stretch)  
**Related:** [input-commands.md](input-commands.md), [ADR-002](../decisions/ADR-002-multiplayer-netcode.md)

---

## Handshake

### `C2S_Join`

```text
{
  type: "join"
  protocolVersion: 1
  sessionId: string
  seatToken: string
  reconnectToken?: string
  clientInfo?: { name?: string, build?: string }
}
```

### `S2C_Welcome`

```text
{
  type: "welcome"
  protocolVersion: 1
  sessionId: string
  seatId: 0|1|2|3
  reconnectToken: string
  rngSeed: number
  rulesetVersion: string
  tickRate: 30
  phase: SessionPhase
  snapshot: WorldSnapshot
}
```

### `S2C_Error`

```text
{
  type: "error"
  code: "PROTOCOL" | "AUTH" | "FULL" | "PHASE" | "INTERNAL"
  message: string
}
```

---

## Client → Server

| Type | Payload | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `C2S_Input` | `{ type, seatId, command: InputCommand }` | Rate-limited; seat must match token |
| `C2S_Ready` | `{ type, ready: bool }` | Lobby / Instructions |
| `C2S_ClaimCharacter` | `{ type, character: CharacterId }` | Lobby; always succeeds for valid id (Q9 soft-unique — duplicates allowed; client may warn) |
| `C2S_Leave` | `{ type }` | Graceful |
| `C2S_Ping` | `{ type, clientTime: number }` | RTT measurement |
| `C2S_EndSkip` | `{ type }` | Skip cinematic segment if allowed |
| `C2S_NameEntry` | `{ type, name: string }` | End high score; validated |

---

## Server → Client

| Type | Payload | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `S2C_Snapshot` | `WorldSnapshot` | Full state MVP each tick or every N ticks |
| `S2C_Event` | `GameEvent` | One-shot SFX/VFX/UI triggers |
| `S2C_PhaseChange` | `{ phase, detail }` | Instructions/Level/Fork/End… |
| `S2C_ScoreReport` | `ScoreReport` | End of run; authoritative |
| `S2C_Pong` | `{ clientTime, serverTime }` | |
| `S2C_SeatUpdate` | `{ seats: SeatPublic[] }` | Join/leave/AI takeover notices |
| `S2C_ForkState` | `{ options, tallies, endsAtTick }` | During fork |
| `S2C_Chat` | optional / out of scope MVP | |

---

## Core payloads

### `SessionPhase`

```text
"lobby" | "instructions" | "level" | "fork" | "end_count"
| "end_shares" | "end_spoils" | "end_entry" | "closed"
```

### `WorldSnapshot`

```text
{
  tick: number
  phase: SessionPhase
  levelId?: string
  levelsCompleted: number
  levelsAfterHoard: number     // run length config (Q8); lets UI render "Level k / n" (delta #4)
  lastProcessedInputSeq: { [seatId: number]: number }
  haulers: HaulerPublic[]
  treasures: TreasurePublic[]
  traps: TrapPublic[]          // dynamic only; static grid may be level-hash
  switches: SwitchPublic[]
  cameraHint?: { x, y, z? }    // optional server suggestion
}
```

### `HaulerPublic`

```text
{
  seatId: number
  character: CharacterId
  control: "human" | "ai"
  x: number
  y: number
  vx: number
  vy: number
  facing: 1 | -1
  anim: AnimState
  carry: { instanceId: string, defId: string }[]
  stunned: bool
  name?: string
}
```

### `GameEvent` (examples)

```text
{ type: "pickup", seatId, instanceId, defId }
{ type: "drop", seatId, instanceId, x, y }
{ type: "throw", seatId, instanceId, vx, vy }
{ type: "spill", seatId, items: [...] }
{ type: "stun", seatId, source }
{ type: "trip", attackerSeatId, targetSeatId }
{ type: "trap_trigger", trapId, kind }
{ type: "level_exit", seatId, order }
{ type: "switch", switchId, pressed: bool }
{ type: "ai_takeover", seatId }
{ type: "human_takeover", seatId }
```

### `ScoreReport`

```text
{
  rulesetVersion: string
  sessionId: string
  totalTreasureGp: number
  players: {
    seatId: number
    character: CharacterId
    human: bool
    modifiers: { id, title, kind, uniqueness, deltaShares }[]
    shares: number              // after min-1 clamp
    sharePercent: number        // 0–100 display
    takeGp: number
    inventoryValueGp: number
    eligibleForHighScore: bool
  }[]
  completionToken: string       // for score submit
  cinema?: EndCinemaData        // presentation-only end cinematic data (accepted delta #2)
  recordFanfareThresholdGp?: number  // top totalHaulGp on board; omit → client skips fanfare (delta #3)
}
```

### `EndCinemaData` (presentation-only; server-authored)

All GP values must match the rules evaluation used for `totalTreasureGp` / takes.
Clients must not re-derive official values from `defId`.

```text
{
  tossOrderSeatIds: number[]     // slowest → fastest (len 4)
  exitOrderSeatIds: number[]     // first exit → last on final level
  players: {
    seatId: number
    items: {
      instanceId: string
      defId: string
      displayName: string
      valueGp: number
      setId?: string
    }[]
  }[]
  setCompletions: {
    setId: string
    displayName: string
    bonusGp: number
    contributorSeatIds: number[]
    completingInstanceId: string   // which toss triggers the popout
  }[]
}
```

---

## Timing & reliability

- Server is source of truth; clients must tolerate lost events by relying on snapshot.
- Events are **not** guaranteed if a client was disconnected; full snapshot on reconnect.
- `lastProcessedInputSeq` drives reconciliation.
- Suggested max message size soft limit: 32 KB JSON snapshot (4 players is tiny).

---

## Anti-cheat surface

| Client claim | Server action |
|---|---|
| Position | Ignored (inputs only) |
| Inventory | Ignored |
| Score | Ignored; `ScoreReport` only |
| Ready | Accepted in lobby/instructions |
| Name | Length/charset filter |

---

## Test contract

Integration tests must cover:

1. Join → Welcome → Snapshot stream  
2. Input seq monotonic handling  
3. Reconnect with token restores seatId + inventory  
4. Protocol mismatch → `S2C_Error PROTOCOL`  
5. Fourth human rejected or queued when seats full (`FULL`)

1	# Contract: Player Input Commands
2	
3	**Producers:** Input Mapper (human), AI Controller  
4	**Consumers:** Netcode Client (transport), Authoritative Simulation  
5	**Related:** Design doc §2.1 Controls; [netcode-messages.md](netcode-messages.md)
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Goals
10	
11	- Single normalized command shape for humans and AI.
12	- Transport-cheap, tick-aligned.
13	- **Server interprets chords** (drop/throw) from axes + buttons to avoid client ambiguity.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## `InputCommand`
18	
19	```text
20	InputCommand {
21	  seq: number           // per-seat monotonic; client-assigned
22	  clientTick?: number   // optional
23	  axes: {
24	    x: -1 | 0 | 1       // run / steer / menu left-right
25	    y: -1 | 0 | 1       // duck/pickup (down), throw aim up, fork select, name entry
26	  }
27	  jump: boolean         // A held or pressed — server uses edge detect
28	  action: boolean       // B
29	  start: boolean        // Start / pause / skip
30	  select?: boolean      // optional Select
31	}
32	```
33	
34	### Encoding notes
35	
36	- Booleans are **level** (down), not only edges; server tracks previous tick for `justPressed`.
37	- `seq` must increase by ≥1; duplicates ignored; gaps tolerated (lossy net).
38	- AI sets `seq` from server-side counter (not over wire as client).
39	
40	---
41	
42	## Context interpretation (server)
43	
44	### Lobby / Title / Menus
45	
46	| Input | Meaning |
47	|---|---|
48	| any face / start | Activate UI focus / start flow |
49	| axes | Navigate lists |
50	
51	### Level / Instructions / Hoard
52	
53	| Input | Meaning |
54	|---|---|
55	| axes.x | Run / air steer |
56	| axes.y down | Duck; if near treasure → pickup attempt |
57	| jump pressed | Jump |
58	| action pressed (empty hands) | Trip / push |
59	| action + axes.y down | Drop first (top) treasure |
60	| action + axes.y up | Throw first treasure |
61	| start | Local pause UI only (MVP); no server freeze |
62	
63	### Fork
64	
65	| Input | Meaning |
66	|---|---|
67	| axes.x or axes.y | Select path (design: up/down — implement consistently; **recommend axes.y** per design, allow axes.x as alias) |
68	| jump or action pressed | “Argue” pulse (+1 to selected path tally) |
69	
70	### End name entry
71	
72	| Input | Meaning |
73	|---|---|
74	| axes.y | Change letter |
75	| axes.x | Change character slot |
76	| jump | Confirm letter / submit when full |
77	| action | Delete character |
78	| start | Skip animation / confirm entry |
79	
80	---
81	
82	## Simulation API (server-internal)
83	
84	```text
85	applyInput(seatId: number, cmd: InputCommand, tick: number): void
86	```
87	
88	- Ignores input if seat stunned (except maybe none).
89	- Ignores movement if phase disallows free-run (Fork/End).
90	- Human takeover: any valid human cmd on AI seat with matching token flips `control` to human (online drop-in).
91	
92	---
93	
94	## Idle / AI takeover thresholds (online adaptation of design)
95	
96	| Condition | Effect |
97	|---|---|
98	| No human packets **20s** | `control → AI` |
99	| No human packets **5s** AND hauler at camera pressure edge | `control → AI` |
100	| Human packet while AI | `control → Human` |
101	
102	Exact edge definition: server camera bounds or exit-direction stuck flag.
103	
104	---
105	
106	## Validation
107	
108	- Reject `axes` outside {-1,0,1}.
109	- Drop commands for wrong seatToken.
110	- Rate limit > tickRate * 2.
111	- Do not trust client chord pretinterpretation messages (none exist).
112	
113	---
114	
115	## Test cases
116	
117	1. Jump edge triggers once per press cycle.  
118	2. Drop only if carry non-empty.  
119	3. Throw imparts velocity matching facing.  
120	4. Stunned seat: movement commands no-op.  
121	5. AI and human command shapes identical in sim unit tests.  
122

# Contract: Player Input Commands

**Producers:** Input Mapper (human), AI Controller  
**Consumers:** Netcode Client (transport), Authoritative Simulation  
**Related:** Design doc §2.1 Controls; [netcode-messages.md](netcode-messages.md)

---

## Goals

- Single normalized command shape for humans and AI.
- Transport-cheap, tick-aligned.
- **Server interprets chords** (drop/throw) from axes + buttons to avoid client ambiguity.

---

## `InputCommand`

```text
InputCommand {
  seq: number           // per-seat monotonic; client-assigned
  clientTick?: number   // optional
  axes: {
    x: -1 | 0 | 1       // run / steer / menu left-right
    y: -1 | 0 | 1       // duck/pickup (down), throw aim up, fork select, name entry
  }
  jump: boolean         // A held or pressed — server uses edge detect
  action: boolean       // B
  start: boolean        // Start / pause / skip
  select?: boolean      // optional Select
}
```

### Encoding notes

- Booleans are **level** (down), not only edges; server tracks previous tick for `justPressed`.
- `seq` must increase by ≥1; duplicates ignored; gaps tolerated (lossy net).
- AI sets `seq` from server-side counter (not over wire as client).

---

## Context interpretation (server)

### Lobby / Title / Menus

| Input | Meaning |
|---|---|
| any face / start | Activate UI focus / start flow |
| axes | Navigate lists |

### Level / Instructions / Hoard

| Input | Meaning |
|---|---|
| axes.x | Run / air steer |
| axes.y down | Duck; if near treasure → pickup attempt |
| jump pressed | Jump |
| action pressed (empty hands) | Trip / push |
| action + axes.y down | Drop first (top) treasure |
| action + axes.y up | Throw first treasure |
| start | Local pause UI only (MVP); no server freeze |

### Fork

| Input | Meaning |
|---|---|
| axes.x or axes.y | Select path (design: up/down — implement consistently; **recommend axes.y** per design, allow axes.x as alias) |
| jump or action pressed | “Argue” pulse (+1 to selected path tally) |

### End name entry

| Input | Meaning |
|---|---|
| axes.y | Change letter |
| axes.x | Change character slot |
| jump | Confirm letter / submit when full |
| action | Delete character |
| start | Skip animation / confirm entry |

---

## Simulation API (server-internal)

```text
applyInput(seatId: number, cmd: InputCommand, tick: number): void
```

- Ignores input if seat stunned (except maybe none).
- Ignores movement if phase disallows free-run (Fork/End).
- Human takeover: any valid human cmd on AI seat with matching token flips `control` to human (online drop-in).

---

## Idle / AI takeover thresholds (online adaptation of design)

| Condition | Effect |
|---|---|
| No human packets **20s** | `control → AI` |
| No human packets **5s** AND hauler at camera pressure edge | `control → AI` |
| Human packet while AI | `control → Human` |

Exact edge definition: server camera bounds or exit-direction stuck flag.

---

## Validation

- Reject `axes` outside {-1,0,1}.
- Drop commands for wrong seatToken.
- Rate limit > tickRate * 2.
- Do not trust client chord pretinterpretation messages (none exist).

---

## Test cases

1. Jump edge triggers once per press cycle.  
2. Drop only if carry non-empty.  
3. Throw imparts velocity matching facing.  
4. Stunned seat: movement commands no-op.  
5. AI and human command shapes identical in sim unit tests.

## Base

- JSON over HTTPS

---

## Lobby / Sessions

### `POST /api/v1/sessions`

Create a private room.

**Request**
```text
{ "displayName?: string", "region?: string" }
```

**Response 201**
```text
{
  "sessionId": string
  "joinCode": string          // short human code, e.g. 6 chars
  "wsUrl": string
  "seats": SeatStatus[4]
  "hostSeatToken": string     // creator auto-claimed seat 0 (or first free)

}
```

### `POST /api/v1/sessions/join`

```text
{ "joinCode": string, "displayName?: string" }
```

**Response 200**
```text
{
  "sessionId": string
  "wsUrl": string
  "seatId": number
  "seatToken": string
  "reconnectToken": string
  "seats": SeatStatus[4]
  "phase": SessionPhase
}
```

**Errors:** `NOT_FOUND`, `FULL`, `CLOSED`

### `GET /api/v1/sessions/:sessionId`

Public lobby view (no tokens).

**Response**
```text
{
  "sessionId": string
  "joinCode": string
  "phase": SessionPhase
  "seats": SeatStatus[4]
  "levelsCompleted": number
  "levelsAfterHoard": number
}
```

### `SeatStatus`

```text
{
  "seatId": number
  "occupied": bool
  "control": "human" | "ai" | "empty"
  "character"?: CharacterId
  "ready": bool
  "displayName"?: string
}
```

### Character claim

Preferred via WS `C2S_ClaimCharacter`. Optional REST:

`POST /api/v1/sessions/:id/claim`  
Headers: `Authorization: Seat <seatToken>`  
Body: `{ "character": CharacterId }`

**Policy (frozen Q9 — soft-unique):** Claim always succeeds for a valid `CharacterId`; seats may share a character. Client may warn when selecting an already-claimed character. `409` is reserved for true conflicts (e.g. double seat bind), never "character taken".

---

## High scores

### `GET /api/v1/highscores`

**Query:** `?limit=25`

**Response**
```text
{
  "top": HighScoreRow[]
  "lastRun"?: {
    "sessionId": string
    "entries": { name?: string, character: CharacterId, takeGp: number, sharePercent: number }[]
  }
  "recentNewIds": string[]    // last three highscore row ids for "New!" tag
}
```

### `HighScoreRow`

```text
{
  "id": string
  "name": string
  "character": CharacterId
  "takeGp": number
  "sharePercent": number
  "totalHaulGp": number
  "createdAt": string  // ISO-8601
}
```

### `POST /api/v1/highscores`

**Request**
```text
{
  "completionToken": string
  "seatId": number
  "name": string
}
```

**Server validation**
1. Token matches completed session `ScoreReport`.  
2. Seat was human.  
3. `eligibleForHighScore` true.  
4. Name: 1–12 chars, allowlist charset.  
5. Single submit per seat/token.

**Response 201:** `HighScoreRow`  
**Errors:** `UNAUTHORIZED`, `CONFLICT`, `VALIDATION`

---

### `GET /health`

```text
{ "ok": true, "version": string, "rooms"?: number }
```

---

## CORS & static

- API may be same-origin with static client or explicit CORS allowlist.  
- Static SPA fallback must not swallow `/api/*` or WS paths (Build Plan warning still applies if reverse-proxied).

---

## Test contract

- Create → join ×3 → fourth join succeeds → fifth `FULL`  
- Join bad code → `NOT_FOUND`  
- Submit score without token → fail  
- Submit twice → `CONFLICT`  
- AI seat submit → fail

1	# ADR-002: Multiplayer & Netcode Approach
2	
3	| Field | Value |
4	|---|---|
5	| Status | **Accepted** (architecture phase) |
6	| Date | 2026-07-20 |
7	| Deciders | Software Game Architect (Dungeon Haul) |
8	| Depends on | [ADR-001](ADR-001-tech-stack.md) |
9	
10	---
11	
12	## Context
13	
14	The original design is a **local drop-in/drop-out** four-player game with AI fill. Product direction expands this to **online multiplayer**.
15	
16	Gameplay involves:
17	
18	- Contentious treasure ownership (spill/steal)  
19	- Trip/push player interactions  
20	- Fork voting by button-mash  
21	- Share modifiers from session-wide stats  
22	- Always **exactly four** active haulers in Game State  
23	
24	Fairness and fun require a clear authority model, reconnection story, and latency strategy.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Decision
29	
30	### Topology
31	
32	**Authoritative dedicated server** (client–server). **Not** peer-to-peer. **Not** listen-server host-among-players.
33	
34	One **HaulSession room** runs one playthrough. The server:
35	
36	1. Accepts `InputCommand` only from clients  
37	2. Steps a **fixed 30 Hz** simulation  
38	3. Broadcasts `WorldSnapshot` + `GameEvent`s  
39	4. Computes end scores via pure Rules package  
40	5. Fills inactive seats with **AI** producing the same input interface  
41	
42	### Client role
43	
44	- Render snapshots  
45	- **Predict** local hauler movement  
46	- **Reconcile** using `lastProcessedInputSeq`  
47	- **Interpolate** remote haulers  
48	- Never authoritatively mutate inventory, scores, or trap state  
49	
50	### Session access
51	
52	- **Private join codes** (MVP)  
53	- Optional public matchmaking (stretch)  
54	- Seat tokens + **reconnect tokens** with grace period (e.g. 30s)  
55	
56	### Drop-in / drop-out
57	
58	Online adaptation of design idle rules:
59	
60	- 20s no input → AI takeover  
61	- 5s no input + edge pressure → AI takeover  
62	- Any input from seat owner → human takeover  
63	- Disconnect → AI pilots during grace; reconnect restores seat  
64

66	
67	Allowed while phase ∈ Lobby, Instructions, Level, Fork. Spawn policy: safe point near average human position or level spawn. End phase: no new fighters (MVP).
68

71	**No host.** Server process owns room. Process death ends room (MVP). Stretch: snapshot migration.
72	
73	### Tick & payloads
74	
75	| Item | MVP |
76	|---|---|
77	| Tick | 30 Hz fixed |
78	| State sync | Full snapshot (small: 4 players) |
79	| Transport | WebSocket JSON |

81	| Prediction | Local player only |
82	
83	### Room framework
84	
85	**Colyseus** for room lifecycle and reconnection patterns; simulation code remains our module invoked from the room.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## Alternatives considered
90	
91	### Peer-to-peer / host migration
92	
93	- Fails host-leave and cheat resistance for steal/trip.  
94	- **Rejected.**
95	
96	### Lockstep deterministic peers
97	
98	- Requires full determinism across browsers; heavy for platformer physics.  
99	- **Rejected** for MVP.
100	
101	### Client-authoritative with server validation
102	
103	- Easier feel; easy to cheat loot.  
104	- **Rejected.**

106	### 60 Hz + rollback (GGPO-style)
107	
108	- Best feel; high engineering cost.  
109	- **Stretch** if playtests demand.

112	
113	- Lower latency potential; NAT and complexity.  
114	- **Stretch** after WS MVP.
115	
116	### Fully serverless per-message functions
117	
118	- Cannot host continuous tick affordably.  
119	- **Rejected** for sim; OK for high-score REST.
120	
121	---
122	
123	## MVP vs stretch
124	
125	| Feature | MVP | Stretch |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| 1–4 remote humans + AI fill | ✅ | |
128	| Join codes | ✅ | Quick play matchmaking |
129	| Reconnect grace | ✅ | Cross-node migration |
130	| Local prediction | ✅ basic | Full rollback |

132	| Same-machine multi-seat online | ❌ | ✅ |
133	| Delta compression / binary | ❌ | ✅ |
134	| Global pause vote | ❌ | ✅ |
135	| Cheat hardening beyond authority | basic | advanced |
136	
137	---

139	## Consequences
140	
141	### Positive
142	
143	- Fair loot and scoring  
144	- AI fill works without special client hacks  
145	- Clear component boundaries (net client vs sim)  
146	- Testable with headless input tapes

151	- Requires hosting cost for game processes

158	- Playtest Session A gates feel before content expansion  
159	- Deploy on sticky process host (Fly.io)

# ADR-002: Multiplayer & Netcode Approach

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | **Accepted** (architecture phase) |
| Date | 2026-07-20 |
| Deciders | Software Game Architect (Dungeon Haul) |
| Depends on | [ADR-001](ADR-001-tech-stack.md) |

---

## Context

The original design is a **local drop-in/drop-out** four-player game with AI fill. Product direction expands this to **online multiplayer**.

Gameplay involves:

- Contentious treasure ownership (spill/steal)  
- Trip/push player interactions  
- Fork voting by button-mash  
- Share modifiers from session-wide stats  
- Always **exactly four** active haulers in Game State  

Fairness and fun require a clear authority model, reconnection story, and latency strategy.

---

## Decision

### Topology

**Authoritative dedicated server** (client–server). **Not** peer-to-peer. **Not** listen-server host-among-players.

One **HaulSession room** runs one playthrough. The server:

1. Accepts `InputCommand` only from clients  
2. Steps a **fixed 30 Hz** simulation  
3. Broadcasts `WorldSnapshot` + `GameEvent`s  
4. Computes end scores via pure Rules package  
5. Fills inactive seats with **AI** producing the same input interface  

### Client role

- Render snapshots  
- **Predict** local hauler movement  
- **Reconcile** using `lastProcessedInputSeq`  
- **Interpolate** remote haulers  
- Never authoritatively mutate inventory, scores, or trap state  

### Session access

- **Private join codes** (MVP)  
- Optional public matchmaking (stretch)  
- Seat tokens + **reconnect tokens** with grace period (e.g. 30s)  

### Drop-in / drop-out

Online adaptation of design idle rules:

- 20s no input → AI takeover  
- 5s no input + edge pressure → AI takeover  
- Any input from seat owner → human takeover  
- Disconnect → AI pilots during grace; reconnect restores seat  

### Mid-join

Allowed while phase ∈ Lobby, Instructions, Level, Fork. Spawn policy: safe point near average human position or level spawn. End phase: no new fighters (MVP).

### Host leave

**No host.** Server process owns room. Process death ends room (MVP). Stretch: snapshot migration.

### Tick & payloads

| Item | MVP |
|---|---|
| Tick | 30 Hz fixed |
| State sync | Full snapshot (small: 4 players) |
| Transport | WebSocket JSON |
| Physics authority | Server AABB + fixed dt |
| Prediction | Local player only |

### Room framework

**Colyseus** for room lifecycle and reconnection patterns; simulation code remains our module invoked from the room.

---

## Alternatives considered

### Peer-to-peer / host migration

- Fails host-leave and cheat resistance for steal/trip.  
- **Rejected.**

### Lockstep deterministic peers

- Requires full determinism across browsers; heavy for platformer physics.  
- **Rejected** for MVP.

### Client-authoritative with server validation

- Easier feel; easy to cheat loot.  
- **Rejected.**

### 60 Hz + rollback (GGPO-style)

- Best feel; high engineering cost.  
- **Stretch** if playtests demand.

### UDP/WebRTC data channels

- Lower latency potential; NAT and complexity.  
- **Stretch** after WS MVP.

### Fully serverless per-message functions

- Cannot host continuous tick affordably.  
- **Rejected** for sim; OK for high-score REST.

---

## MVP vs stretch

| Feature | MVP | Stretch |
|---|---|---|
| 1–4 remote humans + AI fill | ✅ | |
| Join codes | ✅ | Quick play matchmaking |
| Reconnect grace | ✅ | Cross-node migration |
| Local prediction | ✅ basic | Full rollback |
| Spectators | ❌ | ✅ |
| Same-machine multi-seat online | ❌ | ✅ |
| Delta compression / binary | ❌ | ✅ |
| Global pause vote | ❌ | ✅ |
| Cheat hardening beyond authority | basic | advanced |

---

## Consequences

### Positive

- Fair loot and scoring  
- AI fill works without special client hacks  
- Clear component boundaries (net client vs sim)  
- Testable with headless input tapes  

### Negative

- Platforming will feel slightly worse than pure local  
- Requires hosting cost for game processes  
- Must implement prediction carefully to avoid rubber-banding  

### Mitigations

- 30 Hz + prediction on jump/run  
- Generous stun windows slightly mask jitter  
- Playtest Session A gates feel before content expansion  
- Deploy on sticky process host (Fly.io)  

---

## Interface impact

Frozen in:

- [interfaces/netcode-messages.md](../interfaces/netcode-messages.md)  
- [interfaces/input-commands.md](../interfaces/input-commands.md)  
- [interfaces/lobby-and-scores.md](../interfaces/lobby-and-scores.md)  

---

## Validation plan

1. Two-browser movement demo (Implementation Plan P2 gate)  
2. Disconnect/reconnect inventory preserve  
3. Treasure ownership race unit/integration tests  
4. Human playtest “net feel” scores  

---

## Notes on design-doc local multiplayer

Local NES-style multi-gamepad remains desirable later: implement as **multiple seats from one client connection** (stretch) or offline loopback server. Architecture does not require a second simulation codebase.

1	# C-06 — Authoritative Simulation — Design
2	
3	| Field | Value |
4	|---|---|
5	| Component | **C-06 Authoritative Simulation** |
6	| Ownership | **SE-5** (primary); integrates SE-6 Rules, SE-8 AI, SE-7 Levels, C-10 Fork |
7	| Status | Design (documentation only) |
8	| Related | [ARCHITECTURE.md](../../ARCHITECTURE.md) §6–8, [COMPONENTS.md](../../COMPONENTS.md) C-06, [ADR-002](../../decisions/ADR-002-multiplayer-netcode.md) |
9	| Contracts | [netcode-messages.md](../../interfaces/netcode-messages.md), [input-commands.md](../../interfaces/input-commands.md), [share-modifier-api.md](../../interfaces/share-modifier-api.md), [level-format.md](../../interfaces/level-format.md) |
10	| Product locks | [ARCHITECT-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md](../../decisions/ARCHITECT-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md) Q4-A, Q8-A, Q10-A |
11	
12	---
13	
14	## 1. Purpose
15	
16	Own the **server-side truth** for a single `HaulSession` playthrough:
17	
18	- Fixed-timestep world update (movement, gravity, collisions, surface friction)
19	- Treasure lifecycle (seeded spawn, pickup/drop/throw, spill on stun)
20	- Traps, switches, gates, and MVP hazard subset
21	- Always **exactly 4 hauler seats**, human or AI-controlled
22	- Session **phase machine** (Lobby → Instructions → Level/Hoard → Fork → Level… → End → Closed)
23	- Emit `WorldSnapshot` + `GameEvent` streams for netcode
24	- Track `PlayerStats` for Rules Engine share modifiers
25	- Invoke pure Rules only at end-of-run for `ScoreReport`
26	
27	Clients never mutate inventory, scores, trap state, or positions authoritatively. Inputs only.
28	
29	---
30	
31	## 2. Non-goals
32	
33	| Out of scope | Owner |
34	|---|---|
35	| Share title presentation / end cinematics | C-11 |
36	| HTTP lobby, seat tokens, join codes | C-05 |
37	| High-score DB writes | C-12 (sim only produces `ScoreReport` + completion token) |
38	| Drawing, camera, parallax | C-02 |
39	| Pixel-map parse | C-09 (sim consumes `LevelDefinition`) |
40	| AI decision policy internals | C-08 (sim provides read-only view; applies AI `InputCommand` same as human) |
41	| Fork argue UI presentation | C-01/C-02; **tally resolution is C-10**, driven by sim phase |
42	| Global pause that freezes the room | **Forbidden in MVP** (Q10-A) |
43	
44	---
45	
46	## 3. Placement in the system
47	
48	```text
49	Colyseus HaulSession Room
50	  ├── seat auth / reconnect tokens
51	  ├── inbound C2S_Input / Ready / Leave
52	  └── AuthoritativeSimulation  ← this component
53	        ├── PhysicsWorld (AABB, fixed dt)
54	        ├── HaulerSystem (4 seats)
55	        ├── TreasureSystem
56	        ├── TrapSystem
57	        ├── StatsTracker
58	        ├── PhaseMachine
59	        ├── ForkVote (C-10) when phase=fork
60	        ├── AI view adapter → C-08
61	        └── Rules hooks (C-07) at end only
62	```
63	
64	Sim is a **pure-ish module** invoked by the room each tick. Prefer no Phaser, no HTTP, no DB inside sim. Room owns transport; sim owns gameplay state.
65	
66	---
67	
68	## 4. Fixed tick model
69	
70	### 4.1 Parameters
71	
72	| Parameter | MVP value | Notes |
73	|---|---|---|
74	| `tickRate` | **30 Hz** | Published in `S2C_Welcome` |
75	| `dt` | `1/30` s | **Never** use wall-clock dt for physics; no spiral of death |
76	| Input buffer | 2–3 ticks | Late inputs applied on next tick if within window; else drop |
77	| Snapshot | Full `WorldSnapshot` each tick (MVP) | 4 haulers → small payload |
78	| Background clients | Do not drive sim | Server clock only |
79	
80	### 4.2 Tick loop (order)
81	
82	Each tick `t`:
83	
84	1. **Ingest inputs** — drain per-seat queues; reject invalid/wrong-phase; update idle timers  
85	2. **AI fill** — for seats with `control == AI`, request `InputCommand` from C-08 (or cached)  
86	3. **Phase gate** — if phase is non-gameplay (Fork/End/Lobby), skip free-run physics; route to phase handlers  
87	4. **Interpret chords** — drop / throw / trip-push from axes+action (server-side edge detect)  
88	5. **Integrate forces** — gravity, jump impulse, run accel, encumbrance multipliers, surface friction  
89	6. **Resolve collisions** — AABB vs solid grid + dynamic entities  
90	7. **Interactions** — pickup, throw projectiles, trip/push, switch press, trap triggers  
91	8. **Hazard outcomes** — stun, spill, lockout, destroy-in-pit  
92	9. **Exit / phase transitions** — level complete, fork entry, end scoring  
93	10. **Stats** — increment counters (airtime, hits, etc.)  
94	11. **Emit** — build snapshot + events; room broadcasts  
95	
96	### 4.3 Determinism policy
97	
98	- **Rules / scoring:** bit-stable integers given seed + ordered inputs (C-07).  
99	- **Physics:** best-effort deterministic on **one server process** (fixed tick, seeded RNG for rolls). Do **not** require cross-architecture bitwise parity. Tests use input tapes + invariants (ownership, no soft-lock), not multi-machine hash equality.  
100	- Session `rngSeed` from welcome; all treasure rolls and fork pair picks use a single stream (document sub-stream splits if needed).
101	
102	### 4.4 No global pause (Q10-A)
103	
104	- `start` on a client may open a **local** menu only.  
105	- Server **never** freezes ticks for pause.  
106	- No vote-pause in MVP (stretch per ADR-002).  
107	- Fork/End phases slow *gameplay meaning* of inputs without stopping the tick clock (`endsAtTick` still advances).
108	
109	---
110	
111	## 5. World & physics
112	
113	### 5.1 Coordinate space
114	
115	- World units: pixels; **blockSizePx = 32** (assumption until art locks).  
116	- Origin and **y-down** consistent with Phaser and [level-format.md](../../interfaces/level-format.md).  
117	- Hauler AABB and treasure AABBs in world space; grid cells map `cell * blockSizePx`.
118	
119	### 5.2 Hauler kinematics (conceptual)
120	
121	```text
122	HaulerBody {
123	  x, y, vx, vy
124	  halfW, halfH          // duck shortens halfH
125	  grounded: bool
126	  facing: 1 | -1
127	  jumpBufferedUntilTick?
128	  coyoteUntilTick?      // optional feel polish; document if used
129	}
130	```
131	
132	**MVP movement set**
133	
134	| Action | Behavior |
135	|---|---|
136	| Run | Accelerate toward `axes.x * maxSpeed * speedMultiplier` |
137	| Jump | On grounded + jump edge → set `vy` to jump velocity × `jumpMultiplier` |
138	| Air steer | Reduced accel vs ground |
139	| Duck | `axes.y == +1` (down); enables pickup; shrinks hitbox |
140	| Gravity | Constant acceleration while airborne |
141	| Surfaces | Ice: low friction; Sand: high friction / lower max speed; Brick: default |
142	
143	Exact constants live in a **tunable config object** (not magic numbers scattered), shared with client prediction helpers where possible (`packages/rules` or `packages/sim-core` kinematics pure helpers — implementation choice for SE-5; pure helpers preferred for prediction parity).
144	
145	### 5.3 Collision
146	
147	- Static: solid cells from `LevelDefinition.cells` (brick, ice, sand, closed gates, etc.).  
148	- Dynamic: other haulers (push/trip), free treasures, projectiles (thrown items, falling rocks).  
149	- Resolution: discrete sweep or iterative AABB separation; prefer **no tunneling** for hauler-sized bodies at 30 Hz.  
150	- One-way platforms: stretch unless level content requires them for Hoard/BoxLevel.
151	
152	### 5.4 Encumbrance / weight
153	
154	Integrates C-07 `computeEncumbrance(carryCount, carryWeight)`:
155	
156	| Rule | Detail |
157	|---|---|
158	| Free items | First **3** carried treasures: no speed/jump penalty |
159	| Extra items | Cumulative decrease per extra item (and/or weight) |
160	| Floor | `minSpeedMultiplier` may reach **0** (enables Greed Overwhelming) |
161	| Side effects | Weight increases knockback taken, helps heavy switches, can trigger crumbling blocks |
162	
163	Carry stack order: **first element = top** (drop/throw acts on top). Coin sacks may flag `affectsStackVisual: false` but still count for value/weight unless catalog says otherwise — sim follows TreasureDef flags from rules/catalog.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 6. Four seats + AI
168	
169	### 6.1 Seat model
170	
171	Always `seats[0..3]`:
172	
173	```text
174	HaulerSlot {
175	  seatId: 0..3
176	  character: Gnome | Sprite | Halfling | Dwarf
177	  control: "human" | "ai"
178	  humanId?: string
179	  body: HaulerBody
180	  anim: AnimState
181	  carryStack: TreasureInstance[]
182	  weight: number
183	  stunnedUntilTick?: number
184	  pickupLockoutUntilTick?: number
185	  stats: PlayerStats
186	  lastHumanInputTick?: number
187	  lastProcessedSeq: number
188	}
189	```
190	
191	Character soft-unique (Q9-A): prefer distinct; allow clash.
192	
193	### 6.2 Control transitions
194	
195	| Event | Behavior |
196	|---|---|
197	| Human joins empty/AI seat | Soft-takeover: keep position + inventory; `control → human` |
198	| No human packets **20s** | `control → AI` |
199	| No human packets **5s** + camera-edge / exit-stuck pressure | `control → AI` |
200	| Human packet on owned seat while AI | `control → human` |
201	| Disconnect | Grace (e.g. 30s): AI pilots; reconnect restores seat |
202	| Permanent leave | Slot remains AI for rest of run |
203	| Mid-join | Allowed in Lobby, Instructions, Level, Fork; spawn safe (level spawn or near human-average) |
204	| End phase | No new fighters (MVP) |
205	
206	Emit `ai_takeover` / `human_takeover` events; broadcast `S2C_SeatUpdate`.
207	
208	### 6.3 AI integration
209	
210	- C-08 produces synthetic `InputCommand` each tick for AI seats.  
211	- **Identical** apply path as human commands (no teleport, no direct inventory mutate).  
212	- Instructions phase: **AI absent** — empty seats do not receive AI controllers (design fidelity). AI active from **Hoard onward**.  
213	- Sim exposes read-only view: positions, carry counts, max human load, nearby treasure, switches, exit direction.
214	
215	### 6.4 Input application
216	
217	Internal API (from [input-commands.md](../../interfaces/input-commands.md)):
218	
219	```text
220	applyInput(seatId, cmd, tick): void
221	```
222	
223	- Validate axes ∈ {-1,0,1}; seq monotonic (dup ignore, gaps OK).  
224	- Stunned: movement/actions no-op until `stunnedUntilTick`.  
225	- Phase-disallowed free-run: ignore locomotion (Fork/End).  
226	- Rate limit at room edge; sim assumes pre-validated seat ownership.
227	
228	---
229	
230	## 7. Treasure system
231	
232	### 7.1 Spawn
233	
234	- On level load: for each `treasureSlots[]`, roll via C-07 `rollTreasureDef(rng, table, ctx)`.  
235	- World mix target: **65% Common, 20% Rare, 5% Unique, 10% Set** (design).  
236	- Unique/Set: no duplicate **in play**; lost uniques may re-roll later or appear in chests.  
237	- Chests: open interaction rolls secondary table (`wooden_chest` … `magic_chest`).
238	
239	### 7.2 Ownership
240	
241	| Action | Rules |
242	|---|---|
243	| Pickup | Duck near free instance; grant only if not lockout and free; server sole grantor |
244	| Drop | Chord action+down: detach top stack item near feet |
245	| Throw | Chord action+up: detach top with velocity (facing); becomes projectile then free |
246	| Steal | Only via free world instances (after spill/drop/throw), never client claim |
247	| Pit | May **destroy** instance; increment `treasureLostCount` for last owner if tracked |
248	
249	### 7.3 Spill (Sonic-style)
250	
251	On **stun** (trap, severe hit):
252	
253	1. All (or policy subset) carried items detach with outward velocities.  
254	2. Owner gets `pickupLockoutUntilTick` so others can steal.  
255	3. Emit `spill` + `stun` events.  
256	4. Stats: `stunnedOrHurtCount`, `treasureLostCount` as items leave ownership.
257	
258	### 7.4 Conservation invariant
259	
260	- Every `instanceId` is either: carried by one seat, free in world, or destroyed (logged).  
261	- Never two owners. Tests assert this under racey multi-seat pickup tapes.
262	
263	---
264	
265	## 8. Traps, switches, hazards
266	
267	### 8.1 Runtime behaviors (from level cells)
268	
269	| Type | Sim behavior |
270	|---|---|
271	| Spikes | Contact → stun + spill |
272	| Crumbling | Break under mass/time; becomes empty |
273	| Receding | Vanish after step delay |
274	| Lightning cycle / switch | Timed or switched stun zone |
275	| Gas switch | Area stun |
276	| Falling rock spawner | Spawn projectile hazard |
277	| Switch | Pressed while overlapping + grounded → activate linked devices |
278	| Heavy switch | Requires mass ≥ threshold (design: ~3 unloaded players **or** fewer with treasure) |
279	| Golem / Phantom | MVP subset OK; stubs log once if deferred |
280	| Ice / sand | Friction modifiers (not traps) |
281	
282	MVP priority (Implementation Plan P3): **spikes + one timed trap**; switches optional then expand.
283	
284	### 8.2 Trip / push
285	
286	- Action pressed, empty hands, near other hauler → trip/push impulse.  
287	- Emit `trip`; update `hitsDealt` / `hitsTaken`.  
288	- May cause fall into trap → secondary stun/spill.
289	
290	---
291	
292	## 9. Level load & exit
293	
294	### 9.1 Load pipeline
295	
296	1. Room/sim requests `LevelDefinition` from C-09 by `levelId`.  
297	2. Build collision grid, place spawns, roll treasure, reset trap state.  
298	3. Place haulers at `spawns[seatId]` (or mid-join safe point).  
299	4. Preserve inventories across levels (haul continues); reset transient stun/lockout.  
300	5. Set `phase = level`, publish `S2C_PhaseChange` + full snapshot.
301	
302	### 9.2 Exit detection
303	
304	- Hauler AABB overlaps `exit` AABB → mark seat exited; emit `level_exit` with order.  
305	- Track first/last exit for Leader of the Pack / Slowpoke stats.  
306	- **Level complete when all active haulers have exited** (AI included when present).  
307	- Instructions: all **active humans** exit right; AI not spawned.  
308	- Hoard: same exit rule as levels.
309	
310	### 9.3 Progression config
311	
312	```text
313	SessionConfig {
314	  levelsAfterHoard: number   // default 2 (Q8-A); full product 7
315	  // ...
316	}
317	```
318	
319	| Counter | Meaning |
320	|---|---|
321	| `levelsCompleted` | Count of completed **post-Hoard** levels (0 after Hoard exit, before first fork resolution) |
322	| Path after Hoard | Enter Fork; winner chooses next level |
323	| After each post-Hoard level | If `levelsCompleted < levelsAfterHoard` → Fork; else → End |
324	
325	**Hoard** is Level 0 / special; not counted toward `levelsAfterHoard`. Flow:
326	
327	```text
328	Instructions → Hoard → Fork → Level → (Fork → Level)×(levelsAfterHoard-1) → End
329	```
330	
331	With default `levelsAfterHoard = 2`: Hoard → Fork → L1 → Fork → L2 → End.
332	
333	Level pick strategy for forks: **C-10 / Q4-A** — random unplayed pair from pool (see fork-vote DESIGN).
334	
335	---
336	
337	## 10. Phase machine
338	
339	### 10.1 Phases (`SessionPhase`)
340	
341	Aligned with [netcode-messages.md](../../interfaces/netcode-messages.md):
342	
343	```text
344	lobby | instructions | level | fork
345	| end_count | end_shares | end_spoils | end_entry | closed
346	```
347	
348	Note: In-level content includes Hoard; use `levelId` + tags (`pathTags: ["hoard"]`) rather than a separate wire phase if snapshots already carry `levelId`. Architecture state diagram’s `Level0_Hoard` maps to `phase=level` + hoard id.
349	
350	### 10.2 Transitions
351	
352	```mermaid
353	stateDiagram-v2
354	  [*] --> lobby
355	  lobby --> instructions: allReady or forceStart
356	  instructions --> level: all active humans exited\n(load hoard)
357	  level --> fork: level complete AND\n(not end condition)
358	  fork --> level: vote resolved, load next
359	  level --> end_count: levelsCompleted == levelsAfterHoard\n(after post-hoard level complete)
360	  end_count --> end_shares: director / timer
361	  end_shares --> end_spoils
362	  end_spoils --> end_entry: human qualifies
363	  end_spoils --> closed: skip / all done
364	  end_entry --> closed
365	  lobby --> closed: empty TTL
366	```
367	
368	**End condition detail:** After completing a **post-Hoard** level, if `levelsCompleted >= levelsAfterHoard`, go to `end_count` (not Fork). Hoard completion always goes to Fork (unless config short-circuits for tests).
369	
370	### 10.3 Phase-specific sim behavior
371	
372	| Phase | Physics free-run | Inputs used for |
373	|---|---|---|
374	| lobby | No | Ready, claim character (room may handle claim) |
375	| instructions | Yes (limited level) | Movement; no AI |
376	| level | Yes | Full platforming |
377	| fork | **No** free-roam (design) | Path select + argue → **C-10** |
378	| end_* | No | Skip / name entry |
379	| closed | No | None |
380	
381	### 10.4 End scoring handoff
382	
383	On entering `end_count`:
384	
385	1. Freeze inventories (final).  
386	2. Build `ScoreContext` from `PlayerStats` + inventories.  
387	3. Call C-07 `evaluateModifiers` + `computeTakes`.  
388	4. Emit `S2C_ScoreReport` with `completionToken`.  
389	5. Advance end sub-phases on timers or client skip (`C2S_EndSkip`) without re-running rules.
390	
391	---
392	
393	## 11. PlayerStats tracking
394	
395	Sim increments counters continuously (ARCHITECTURE §8). Minimum set for modifiers:
396	
397	- Exit order per level → `exitsFirstCount`, `exitsLastCount`, Leader/Slowpoke flags  
398	- `treasureRecoveredValue`, `treasureLostCount`, `itemsHauledCount`, `setPiecesRecovered`  
399	- `airTimeTicks`, `groundTimeTicks`  
400	- `trapsHit`, `hitsDealt`, `hitsTaken`, `stunnedOrHurtCount`  
401	- `humanControlTicks`, `aiControlTicks`, `controlSwaps`  
402	- `hoardExitItemCount`, `finalItemCount`  
403	- Booleans: `onlyChestsRecovered`, `onlyCommonRecovered`, `speedZeroFromWeight`, `goatOnPole`  
404	
405	Snapshot may omit full stats; end path uses internal full state.
406	
407	---
408	
409	## 12. Outputs to netcode
410	
411	### 12.1 Per-tick
412	
413	- `WorldSnapshot` — tick, phase, levelId, levelsCompleted, haulers, treasures, dynamic traps/switches, `lastProcessedInputSeq`  
414	- Zero or more `GameEvent`s (pickup, drop, throw, spill, stun, trip, trap_trigger, level_exit, switch, takeovers…)
415	
416	### 12.2 Phase / fork / end
417	
418	- `S2C_PhaseChange`  
419	- `S2C_ForkState` (produced with C-10)  
420	- `S2C_ScoreReport`  
421	- `S2C_SeatUpdate`
422	
423	### 12.3 Anti-cheat
424	
425	Ignore client position/inventory/score claims. Inputs only. Documented in netcode contract.
426	
427	---
428	
429	## 13. Public internal interfaces (conceptual)
430	
431	```text
432	// Constructed per room
433	createSimulation(config: SessionConfig, deps: {
434	  loadLevel: (id) => LevelDefinition
435	  rules: RulesApi
436	  ai: AiController
437	  fork: ForkVoteModule   // C-10
438	  nowTick: () => number  // or sim owns tick counter
439	}): Simulation
440	
441	Simulation {
442	  tick(): { snapshot: WorldSnapshot, events: GameEvent[] }
443	  applyInput(seatId, cmd): void
444	  setReady(seatId, ready): void
445	  bindHuman(seatId, humanId): void
446	  releaseHuman(seatId, reason): void
447	  getPhase(): SessionPhase
448	  getScoreReport(): ScoreReport | null
449	  getReadOnlyView(): SimView   // for AI
450	}
451	```
452	
453	Exact TypeScript shapes live in `packages/protocol` / server modules at implementation time — this design freezes **behavior**, not file paths.
454	
455	---
456	
457	## 14. Configuration surface
458	
459	```text
460	SessionConfig {
461	  tickRate: 30
462	  levelsAfterHoard: 2              // Q8-A default; 7 for full
463	  rngSeed: number
464	  rulesetVersion: string
465	  humanIdleAiMs: 20_000
466	  humanIdleEdgeAiMs: 5_000
467	  reconnectGraceMs: 30_000         // room-owned; sim gets control flip events
468	  encumbrance: EncumbranceConfig   // from rules defaults
469	  stunTicks: number
470	  pickupLockoutTicks: number
471	  allowGlobalPause: false          // Q10-A locked
472	  levelPool: string[]              // ids for Q4-A unplayed selection (via C-10)
473	  startLevelId: "hoard_01"
474	}
475	```
476	
477	---
478	
479	## 15. Dependencies
480	
481	| Depends on | Usage |
482	|---|---|
483	| C-07 Rules | Encumbrance helpers; end `evaluateModifiers` / `computeTakes`; treasure roll tables |
484	| C-08 AI | Synthetic inputs for AI seats |
485	| C-09 Levels | `LevelDefinition` load |
486	| C-10 Fork | Vote window, tally, next `levelId` |
487	| `packages/protocol` | Wire snapshot/event types |
488	
489	| Depended on by | Usage |
490	|---|---|
491	| Room / C-05 | Hosts sim; seats |
492	| C-04 clients | Snapshots |
493	| C-12 | Completion token from report |
494	| C-14 | Tick budget metrics |
495	
496	---
497	
498	## 16. Testing strategy (sim-owned)
499	
500	| Layer | Cases |
501	|---|---|
502	| Headless tick driver | Input tapes → assert positions, ground, no NaN |
503	| Ownership | Dual-seat simultaneous pickup → single owner |
504	| Spill | Stun empties stack + lockout allows peer pickup |
505	| Weight | 4th item reduces speed; 0 speed flag for stats |
506	| Phase | Hoard complete → fork; after N levels → end |
507	| AI seat | AI commands move hauler; instructions have no AI |
508	| Idle takeover | 20s silence → AI; human packet returns control |
509	| Pause | `start` does not stop tick counter / peer motion |
510	| Config | `levelsAfterHoard=2` ends after second post-hoard level |
511	| Conservation | Instance IDs accounted for every tick |
512	
513	Golden paths feed Implementation Plan gates G3–G5.
514	
515	---
516	
517	## 17. Risks & mitigations
518	
519	| Risk | Mitigation |
520	|---|---|
521	| Platforming feel over net | Shared kinematics helpers for prediction; generous stun windows |
522	| Treasure races | Server-only grants + lockout |
523	| Scope of traps | MVP subset; stubs for rest |
524	| Physics non-determinism | Single authority; invariant tests |
525	| Phase edge cases (mid-join at exit) | Explicit join spawn + exit set membership rules |
526	| Pause confusion | Docs + no server pause path |
527	
528	---
529	
530	## 18. Implementation notes for SE-5
531	
532	1. Build **headless first** (P2 movement box level) before treasure.  
533	2. Keep phase machine explicit (table/state object), not scattered `if` soup.  
534	3. Delegate fork resolution entirely to C-10; sim only switches phase and loads level.  
535	4. Never import Phaser on server.  
536	5. Default `levelsAfterHoard = 2`; read from room/session create options.  
537	6. Coordinate with SE-6 on encumbrance config object identity.  
538	7. Coordinate with SE-8 on `SimView` minimal surface to avoid AI cheating APIs.
539	
540	---
541	
542	## 19. Traceability
543	
544	| Requirement | Section |
545	|---|---|
546	| Fixed 30 Hz tick | §4 |
547	| Physics / surfaces | §5 |
548	| Weight after 3 items | §5.4 |
549	| Traps | §8 |
550	| Treasure spill | §7.3 |
551	| 4 seats + AI | §6 |
552	| Phase machine | §10 |
553	| levelsAfterHoard default 2 | §9.3, §14 |
554	| No global pause | §4.4 |
555	| Q4-A level pairs | §9.3 → C-10 |
556	| Snapshots / events | §12 |
557	| PlayerStats | §11 |
